items.description: Analyze repository structure and tooling capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/repo_analysis.json` documenting: (1) all modules in `.archivara/` and `.opencode/` with their purposes, (2) the ConceptEvolve pipeline (evolve/probe/reframe/walk) and how sub-agents are dispatched, (3) the Semantic Scholar integration and BibTeX export capability, (4) the agent hierarchy (orchestrator, researcher, writer, reviewer, concept_worker) and their tool permissions, (5) the `results/concept_evolve/tree/` folder convention for concept cards. Must be valid JSON with at least 5 top-level sections.

items.description: DEFLATE format deep-dive: map the sequential dependency chain
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/001_deflate_format_analysis/concept.json` containing: (1) formal description of DEFLATE's three block types (uncompressed, fixed Huffman, dynamic Huffman), (2) bit-level diagram of the decode loop's sequential dependency chain (peek -> table lookup -> consume -> output -> repeat), (3) quantified critical-path latency per symbol on modern x86 (Skylake/Zen4) and ARM (M1/M4) citing cycle counts from Agner Fog or vendor manuals, (4) identification of the three serialization barriers (Huffman variable-length codes, LZ77 back-reference data dependency, bit-stream position tracking). Must cite at least 3 sources.

items.description: Literature review: web search for DEFLATE decompression optimization papers and implementations
items.acceptance_criteria: Using web search tools, locate and summarize at least 15 relevant sources covering: (a) optimized CPU implementations (zlib-ng, libdeflate, ISA-L, zlib-rs, zlib-cloudflare, zlib-chromium, WUFFS, fdeflate, dougallj's zlib fork), (b) parallel decompression (pugz, rapidgzip, pigz), (c) GPU approaches (nvCOMP/GDeflate, CUHD massively parallel Huffman), (d) hardware accelerators (Intel QAT, FPGA implementations), (e) foundational bit-IO and Huffman optimization (Fabian Giesen's series, Yann Collet's Huff0/FSE). Produce `results/concept_evolve/literature_review.json` with an array of objects each containing: title, authors, year, venue, url, category (cpu/parallel/gpu/hardware/foundational), key_insight (1-2 sentences), and relevance_score (1-10).

items.description: Build sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: Create and maintain `sources.bib` in the repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 10 relevant papers and technical references. Must include entries for: RFC 1951 (Deutsch 1996), pugz (Kerbiriou & Chikhi 2019), rapidgzip (Knespel & Brunst 2023), massively parallel Huffman on GPUs (Weissenberger & Schmidt 2018), at least one ISA-L paper, at least one FPGA DEFLATE paper, and at least 4 additional sources. Each entry must have title, author, year, and either doi or url fields. Use Semantic Scholar bibtex export where available.

items.description: Concept-tree exploration: run ConceptEvolve to generate cross-domain concept cards for DEFLATE speedup
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute ConceptEvolve `evolve` with the topic 'Making DEFLATE decompression 2-5x faster than any existing implementation'. Verify that `results/concept_evolve/tree/` contains at least 8 concept folders, each with `concept.json` and `README.md`. Verify `results/concept_evolve/concept_cards.json` exists with at least 8 cards. Verify `results/concept_evolve/semantic_bridge.json` has nodes and edges. Verify `results/concept_evolve/tree/index.json` and `results/concept_evolve/tree/adjacency.json` exist. Delegate to a literature-graph-miner subagent to cross-reference the concept cards against the literature review and annotate each card with supporting citations.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer for traversal, literature-graph-miner for citation cross-referencing

items.description: Competitive landscape analysis: benchmark claims and throughput comparison matrix
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/002_competitive_landscape/concept.json` containing a structured comparison matrix of all known DEFLATE decompression implementations with columns: name, language, single_core_throughput_MBps (on Silesia corpus or equivalent), parallelism_support, SIMD_usage, streaming_api, format_compatibility, license. Must include at least 10 implementations. Include a 'gap_analysis' field identifying the specific performance gaps between stock zlib (~250 MB/s), best single-core (~1100 MB/s libdeflate), and best parallel (~10 GB/s rapidgzip). Cite throughput numbers to specific benchmark sources.

items.description: Establish benchmarking infrastructure and corpus selection
items.acceptance_criteria: Create `results/concept_evolve/tree/003_benchmark_infra/concept.json` specifying: (1) benchmark corpus selection with rationale (must include Silesia corpus, Canterbury corpus, at least one large gzip file >1GB, PNG test suite, and synthetic worst-case inputs), (2) measurement methodology (wall-clock time, CPU cycles via perf/RDTSC, throughput in MB/s of decompressed output, L1/L2/L3 cache miss rates, branch misprediction rates), (3) statistical rigor requirements (minimum 10 runs, report median and p95, exclude first run for warmup), (4) hardware specification template (CPU model, frequency, cache sizes, memory bandwidth). Produce a `benchmarks/` folder specification with planned scripts.

items.description: Profile zlib reference implementation to identify hotspots
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/004_zlib_profiling/concept.json` with a detailed profile of zlib's inflate path showing: (1) percentage of time in each major function (inflate, inflate_fast, updatewindow, adler32, code table building), (2) branch misprediction hotspots with specific line numbers, (3) cache behavior analysis (table sizes, access patterns), (4) IPC measurement showing actual vs. theoretical throughput, (5) comparison of zlib's inflate_fast vs. the main inflate loop. Include profiling methodology and specific perf counters used. Reference prior work from literature review (item_003).

items.description: Baseline throughput measurements across all reference implementations
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/005_baseline_measurements/concept.json` with measured decompression throughput (MB/s) for at least 5 implementations (zlib, zlib-ng, libdeflate, ISA-L, and one Rust implementation) on the benchmark corpus from item_007. Each measurement must include: mean, median, stddev, p95 throughput, and the hardware platform used. Results must be presented as a comparison table and must validate or contradict throughput claims from the literature review (item_003). Include a 'target_throughput' field defining the specific 2x and 5x targets relative to the best measured baseline.
items.notes: Depends on item_007 (benchmark infrastructure) and item_003 (literature throughput claims)

items.description: Micro-benchmark the four critical bottleneck stages independently
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/006_microbenchmarks/concept.json` with isolated micro-benchmarks for: (1) Huffman table construction time (dynamic blocks of varying code-length distributions), (2) Huffman symbol decode throughput (symbols/second for various code-length distributions, measuring the 6-7 cycle critical path), (3) LZ77 copy throughput (varying distances 1-32768 and lengths 3-258, with and without SIMD chunk copy), (4) bit-buffer refill overhead (conditional vs. unconditional refill, measuring branch misprediction cost). Each micro-benchmark must report cycles per operation and identify which stage dominates for typical (Silesia) vs. adversarial inputs. Delegate to a concept-tree-explorer subagent to map these bottleneck measurements to the concept tree and identify which concepts address which bottlenecks.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer to map bottlenecks to concept cards

items.description: Roofline model for DEFLATE decompression throughput limits
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/007_roofline_model/concept.json` containing: (1) a roofline analysis relating decompression throughput to compute intensity (operations per byte) and memory bandwidth, (2) theoretical single-core throughput ceiling derived from: CPU frequency, IPC limit, critical-path cycles per symbol, average symbols per byte of output, (3) theoretical multi-core throughput ceiling derived from: memory bandwidth, output bandwidth, number of cores, (4) identification of which regime (compute-bound or memory-bound) each optimization approach operates in, (5) specific numerical targets: what cycles/symbol and IPC would be needed to achieve 2x and 5x over libdeflate. Must reference the micro-benchmark results from item_010.
items.notes: Depends on item_010 (micro-benchmarks) for empirical cycle counts

items.description: Novel approach 1: Speculative multi-symbol Huffman decode with rollback
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/008_speculative_multisymbol/concept.json` with: (1) detailed algorithm design for speculatively decoding 2-4 Huffman symbols in parallel from a single bit-buffer state by pre-computing conditional decode tables (if symbol 1 is N bits, symbol 2 starts at offset N), (2) analysis of the table size explosion (15^k entries for k speculative symbols) and practical strategies to limit it (restrict to short codes, use prediction), (3) rollback mechanism when speculation fails, (4) expected speedup calculation based on the roofline model from item_011, (5) comparison to Fabian Giesen's multi-stream approach and Oodle's 3-stream interleaving, explaining why this approach works within standard DEFLATE format constraints. Must cite at least 3 papers from sources.bib.
items.notes: Depends on item_011 (roofline model) for speedup estimation

items.description: Novel approach 2: Hybrid parallel decomposition with speculative block finding
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/009_hybrid_parallel/concept.json` with: (1) algorithm combining rapidgzip-style speculative block boundary detection with libdeflate-quality per-block decompression, (2) design for a work-stealing scheduler that dynamically balances block-level parallelism across N cores, (3) analysis of the false-positive rate and its impact on throughput (quantified from pugz/rapidgzip results), (4) strategy for handling single-block files (the worst case for block-level parallelism), (5) design for an optional pre-computed block index that eliminates speculation overhead for repeated decompression of the same file. Must compare quantitatively against rapidgzip's published results. Delegate to a literature-graph-miner subagent to mine the citation graph of Knespel & Brunst 2023 for additional parallel decompression techniques.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner on rapidgzip citation graph

items.description: Novel approach 3: SIMD-accelerated branchless decode loop for modern microarchitectures
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/010_simd_branchless_decode/concept.json` with: (1) design for a branchless inner decode loop using SIMD gather instructions (VPGATHERDD on AVX2, or ARM SVE equivalent) to perform parallel table lookups for the literal/length/distance classification, (2) analysis of using SIMD shuffle-based multi-byte copy for LZ77 back-references (handling the overlapping-copy case with SIMD), (3) design for a 'fast path' that detects sequences of short-code literals and decodes them without per-symbol branching (extending dougallj's fast-path literal technique to decode 4-8 literals per iteration using SIMD), (4) cycle count analysis comparing the branchless SIMD path vs. scalar path on Zen4 and Apple M4, (5) fallback strategy for code distributions that defeat the fast path. Must cite dougallj's work and ISA-L's multi-byte decode approach.

items.description: Novel approach 4: Bit-stream preprocessing for intra-block parallelism
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/011_bitstream_preprocessing/concept.json` with: (1) design for a lightweight first pass that scans a DEFLATE block's bitstream and records Huffman symbol boundaries (bit offsets) without fully decoding, exploiting the self-synchronization property of prefix codes, (2) analysis of the first-pass cost vs. the parallelism it enables (can the boundary scan be done faster than full decode?), (3) design for a second pass that uses the boundary information to decode symbols in parallel chunks, (4) handling of LZ77 data dependencies in the second pass (which copies can be resolved independently?), (5) comparison to GDeflate's bit-swizzling approach -- this approach preserves standard DEFLATE format but adds a runtime preprocessing step. Must quantify the theoretical speedup vs. preprocessing overhead.

items.description: Novel approach 5: Adaptive decode strategy with runtime profiling
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/012_adaptive_decode/concept.json` with: (1) design for a decoder that profiles the first K symbols of each block and selects from multiple decode kernels: (a) fast-path all-literals kernel, (b) short-code-dominated kernel with larger root tables, (c) general kernel for complex code distributions, (d) parallel kernel for blocks exceeding a size threshold, (2) the profiling heuristics and switching criteria (code length histogram, literal vs. match ratio, block size), (3) expected overhead of the profiling step vs. speedup from specialization, (4) analysis of how this compares to WUFFS's compile-time specialization and ISA-L's runtime CPU dispatch. Must connect to at least 2 concept cards from the ConceptEvolve tree (item_005).

items.description: Concept-tree synthesis: identify the highest-value concept paths and prune low-impact directions
items.acceptance_criteria: Run ConceptEvolve `walk` on the concept tree from item_005 and produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/013_synthesis/concept.json` containing: (1) the top 5 concept paths ranked by estimated impact (based on roofline analysis from item_011), (2) for each path, a concrete implementation plan with estimated person-days of effort, (3) a dependency graph showing which novel approaches (items 012-016) depend on which concept cards, (4) identification of at least 2 'blind spot' areas where the concept tree has no coverage but the literature review suggests opportunities, (5) a prioritized roadmap ordering the approaches by expected return on effort. Delegate to a concept-tree-explorer subagent to traverse the full tree and identify missing cross-domain connections.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer for full tree traversal and gap analysis

items.description: Experiment 1: Implement and benchmark the speculative multi-symbol decode (approach 1)
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/014_exp_speculative/concept.json` with: (1) implementation in C or Rust of the speculative multi-symbol Huffman decode from item_012, (2) benchmark results on the Silesia corpus comparing against libdeflate and ISA-L baselines from item_009, (3) measurements of: throughput (MB/s), cycles per symbol, table memory usage, speculation success rate (% of iterations where all speculated symbols were correct), (4) analysis of which file types benefit most vs. least from speculation, (5) statistical significance test (p < 0.05) for any claimed speedup. Results must reference the roofline predictions from item_011.

items.description: Experiment 2: Implement and benchmark hybrid parallel decomposition (approach 2)
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/015_exp_parallel/concept.json` with: (1) implementation of the hybrid parallel decompressor from item_013 supporting 1-N cores, (2) scaling analysis showing throughput vs. core count (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 cores) on at least 3 files of different sizes (1MB, 100MB, 1GB), (3) comparison against rapidgzip on the same files and hardware, (4) measurement of parallel efficiency (speedup / core_count) and identification of the scaling bottleneck, (5) analysis of the impact of block size distribution on parallel efficiency (many small blocks vs. few large blocks). Must achieve at least 2x over best single-core baseline on 4+ cores for files >= 100MB.

items.description: Experiment 3: Implement and benchmark SIMD branchless decode (approach 3)
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/016_exp_simd/concept.json` with: (1) implementation of the SIMD branchless decode loop from item_014 targeting AVX2 (x86-64) and NEON (AArch64), (2) benchmark results on the Silesia corpus comparing against libdeflate scalar path, (3) measurements of: branch misprediction rate reduction (via perf counters), IPC improvement, throughput improvement, (4) analysis of the 'fast path hit rate' -- what percentage of decode iterations use the SIMD fast path vs. falling back to scalar, (5) identification of file characteristics that maximize/minimize SIMD benefit. Compare quantitatively against dougallj's reported speedups.

items.description: Experiment 4: Combined approach -- integrate best-performing techniques
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/017_exp_combined/concept.json` with: (1) implementation combining the best-performing techniques from experiments 1-3 into a single decoder, (2) benchmark results showing the combined throughput vs. each technique in isolation (do they stack?), (3) comparison against ALL baselines from item_009 on the full corpus, (4) analysis of interaction effects (does SIMD branchless decode conflict with speculative multi-symbol?), (5) final throughput numbers with confidence intervals, demonstrating whether the 2-5x target over stock zlib is achieved, and quantifying the speedup over the best existing implementation (libdeflate or ISA-L). Must include results on at least 5 different file types (text, binary, PNG, git pack, synthetic). Delegate to a literature-graph-miner subagent to find any recent (2024-2026) papers that may have attempted similar combinations.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner for recent combination approaches. Depends on items 018-020

items.description: Ablation study: quantify individual contribution of each optimization
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/018_ablation/concept.json` with: (1) ablation study removing one optimization at a time from the combined decoder (item_021) and measuring the throughput impact, (2) a stacked bar chart specification showing the additive contribution of each technique, (3) analysis of which optimizations are complementary vs. redundant, (4) identification of the single most impactful optimization and the 'diminishing returns' point, (5) comparison of the ablation results against the predictions from the roofline model (item_011) -- were the theoretical predictions accurate?

items.description: Edge case and adversarial input evaluation
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/019_adversarial/concept.json` with: (1) correctness verification against the zlib test suite and a DEFLATE conformance test suite, (2) performance on adversarial inputs: maximum-length Huffman codes (15-bit), blocks with only back-references, blocks with only literals, distance-1 run-length encoded data, zip bombs, (3) comparison of adversarial-case throughput against baselines (does the novel decoder degrade worse or better than libdeflate/ISA-L on pathological inputs?), (4) memory safety analysis (no buffer overflows, no undefined behavior under any valid DEFLATE input), (5) fuzzing results (at least 1 hour of AFL/libFuzzer coverage with no crashes).

items.description: Comprehensive results analysis and comparison against prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/020_final_analysis/concept.json` with: (1) summary table of all experimental results from Phase 4, (2) direct quantitative comparison against every implementation from the competitive landscape (item_006), (3) analysis of where the novel approaches succeeded vs. fell short of the 2-5x target, (4) identification of the remaining performance gap to the theoretical roofline from item_011, (5) discussion of which optimizations are format-compatible (standard DEFLATE) vs. require format extensions, (6) citations to at least 8 papers from sources.bib with specific comparisons to their reported results. Delegate to a concept-tree-explorer subagent to traverse the complete concept tree one final time and produce a 'lessons learned' annotation for each concept card.
items.notes: Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer for final tree annotation. Depends on all Phase 4 items

items.description: Write technical report synthesizing all findings
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/021_technical_report/report.md` (Markdown) containing: (1) Abstract (200 words), (2) Introduction with motivation and problem statement, (3) Background covering DEFLATE format and prior optimization work (citing sources.bib), (4) Methodology describing the benchmark setup and novel approaches, (5) Results with tables and figure references for all experiments, (6) Discussion analyzing why each approach worked or failed, (7) Related Work section comparing against at least 10 cited implementations, (8) Conclusion with concrete recommendations for which approach to deploy in different contexts (single-core latency-sensitive, throughput-oriented multi-core, embedded/constrained). Total length: 3000-6000 words.

items.description: Produce visualization specifications for key results
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce specifications in `figures/` for at least 4 figures: (1) `throughput_comparison.json` -- bar chart of all implementations' throughput on Silesia corpus, (2) `scaling_analysis.json` -- line plot of parallel throughput vs. core count, (3) `ablation_waterfall.json` -- waterfall chart showing cumulative impact of each optimization, (4) `roofline_overlay.json` -- roofline diagram with each implementation plotted showing compute vs. memory boundedness. Each specification must include: chart_type, data_source (referencing specific concept.json files), axis_labels, title, and a data array with the actual values to plot.

items.description: Future work roadmap and open problems
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce `results/concept_evolve/tree/022_future_work/concept.json` with: (1) at least 5 concrete open problems identified during this research (e.g., intra-block parallelism without preprocessing, hardware-software co-design for DEFLATE, applying techniques to Brotli/Zstd), (2) for each open problem: estimated difficulty, potential impact, suggested approach, and relevant citations from sources.bib, (3) a 'technology transfer' section identifying which findings are immediately deployable in existing systems (zlib drop-in replacement, nginx module, PNG decoder, Git), (4) analysis of whether the DEFLATE format should be superseded vs. optimized further, citing the ecosystem lock-in argument. Must reference at least 3 concept cards from the tree that were not fully explored.
